overview: Many Americans apply for passports at "acceptance facilities" such as post offices and local government offices, which check the paperwork and keep a small processing fee. This bill would let the State Department also authorize public libraries that are run as nonprofits, charities, or trusts, rather than by a government, to serve as passport acceptance facilities and keep that fee, as long as they follow State Department rules. Within 30 days of the bill becoming law, the department would have to reauthorize any such library that already served as an acceptance facility and was following the rules, and report to Congress on whether it did so. As of July 27, 2026, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it without changes and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say libraries are convenient, trusted places for people to apply for passports, and this restores a service some communities relied on.
against: Critics say expanding passport acceptance to private nonprofit organizations could make oversight of the application process harder for the State Department.
